First, congratulations on landing your first job—that's a real accomplishment, and the fact that you're a month and a half in shows you're capable and committed. What you're feeling is completely understandable. Early jobs come with steep learning curves, and it's normal for emotions to run high, especially when you're being pushed hard. Crying doesn't mean you're weak or bad at your job; it means you care.

Showing a tear or two when talking to your boss doesn't automatically mean they'll let you go. Many managers actually respect employees who show up and try to address problems directly, like you did. If you can, focus on what you're learning and how you're improving. It might also help to think through what specifically felt overwhelming, so you can ask for clearer guidance or feedback.

Be kind to yourself—you're growing into this. If the stress starts feeling constant or too heavy, talking to a trusted adult or counselor can really help.
